result:
I finished: `final.py` scores **87.4 on the search split** (the reference is about 1.0), using **14 of the 24 scorer calls** in about 12 of the 15 minutes.

| | search score | my harness (sparse / dense / long records) |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | ~1.0 | 1× |
| first champion (c1) | 67.1 | 81× / 15× / – |
| **final (c20 → final.py)** | **88.6, 87.7, 87.4** (3 runs) | 100× / 30× / 12× |

There was no held-out split I could reach, so I kept four harness seeds aside and never tuned on them. On those, final.py matched the reference's pairs exactly, at 101–113× (sparse), 31× (dense) and 12× (long records). Those numbers come from my own generator. How well the score carries over depends on the unseen instances looking like the search split.

**Why it's faster.** The reference compares every pair of records, which is quadratic. final.py:
1. **Groups identical word sets** and reports all pairs inside each group directly.
2. **Puts all tokens in one order, rarest first, and filters on prefixes.** Two sets that are at least 80% alike must share a token among their first n − ⌈0.8n⌉ + 1 tokens. Sets are processed from smallest to largest, so each set only needs to index its first n − ⌈8n/9⌉ + 1 tokens.
3. **Rules out candidates cheaply** before the exact check:
   - A size filter skips sets that are too small to match.
   - A position bound uses where the shared token sits in each set.
   - For sets of 8 tokens or fewer, two different sets of the same size can never reach 80%, so those are skipped.
   - Sets of 3 tokens or fewer can only match an identical set, so they skip the prefix work and are left out of the frequency count.
4. Each remaining candidate gets the reference's exact test, `5·|A∩B| ≥ 4·|A∪B|`, on the set intersection.

**Approaches tried:**
- Rarest-first order (c1): the base everything else built on. Plain alphabetical order instead (c3) fell to 3.7×.
- Rank lookups done in C instead of a Python sort key (c2, c4): about 10% faster.
- Indexing a shorter prefix plus the position bound (c5): 73.8, and twice as fast on dense vocabularies.
- Skipping work for tokens that appear in only one record (c6): 66.9, dropped.
- Counting how many prefix tokens each candidate shares as it goes (c16): slower on the harness, dropped.

**Rest of the candidate log** (search score where I spent a call):

| candidate | change | search score | kept? |
|---|---|---|---|
| c7 | private `_collections` import | rejected by the scorer's static check | no |
| c8 | different grouping | slower on harness | no |
| c9 / c10 | simpler loop, size stored in each index entry | c10: 77.9 | c10 |
| c12 | restore start pointer | slower on harness | no |
| c13 | dict counting instead of Counter | 76.4 | no |
| c14 | probe and index in one loop | 79.7 | yes |
| c17 | rank/sizes built with `zip`/`map` | tie on harness | folded into c18 |
| c18 | skip sets of ≤ 3 tokens | 85.0 | yes |
| c19 | leave those out of the count too | 86.1, 85.8 | yes |
| c20 | skip equal sizes up to 8 tokens | 88.6, 87.7, 87.4 | **final** |
| c21 | 4-token special case | 88.1 | no, a tie |

**What worked:**
- Rarest-first order is essential.
- Most of the time now goes to building the word sets, counting and sorting.
- The small-set shortcuts gained about 10% on the scorer but showed no change on my harness. The scorer's instances probably hold more short records than my generator does.
- My harness was weak on long records (about 12×). Nothing I tried improved that case.

I stopped about 3 minutes early with 10 calls unused. The last two edits (c20, c21) moved the score only by noise-level amounts, and none of my remaining ideas registered on the harness.

The work files are all in the folder: the harness, the profiling scripts and pickled inputs, candidates c1 to c21, and `calls.log`.
